blocks.c: Dawn in that room was a strip of light along the bottom of a blind, and it took about four seconds, and nothing else happened at all.

No thunder. No screaming. The lease renewed the way leases renew, which is to say that a date passed and a document remained in force, and the only sign of it was that the stack of paper behind the counter got very slightly shorter, as though a sheet had gone from the top.
"Renewed," said the clerk. "Term: fifty-one years. Caretakers in occupation: two. Accounts settled: none. Disputes held: forty-one thousand, two hundred and six."
Wen sat down on the floor.

She did it the way people do when their legs simply finish, sliding down the front of the counter with her back to it, and she put her hands over her face and made a sound I am not going to write down, because some things you don't put in a log.
I stayed standing, because one of us had to, and because I had one more thing to do and about four seconds of nerve left in which to do it.

"Mrs. Dalisay is on Hendry Street with a signed and dated statement. The renewal is done, so she can enter the premises without being party to it. She'll be at her desk in nine minutes because she is always at her desk by five past and she has been for twenty-two years." I picked up my pen. "Three parties, all present, all able to sign. I'd like to determine forty-one thousand disputes, please. We can start with the coffee."
